title: Eddie Crowder: OU Quarterback Who Led Colorado Football
question: Which former Oklahoma quarterback became Colorado's head football coach and athletic director?
answer: Eddie Crowder, an All-American quarterback for Bud Wilkinson's Sooners in 1952, became Colorado's head coach in 1963 and also served as the school's athletic director from 1965 to 1984.
summary: Eddie Crowder quarterbacked Bud Wilkinson's Sooners to an All-America 1952 season, then coached Colorado to a 67-49-2 record and ran its athletic department.
body: Few Sooners have gone on to shape another major program the way Eddie Crowder did. The quarterback learned the game under Bud Wilkinson, then carried that education to Boulder, Colorado.

Crowder was a reserve quarterback on Oklahoma's 1950 national championship team. He took over as the starter for the next two seasons, with the Sooners going 8-2 in 1951 and 8-1-1 in 1952. As a senior in 1952 he earned All-America and All-Big Seven recognition.

Colorado hired him on January 3, 1963, as the 17th head coach in program history. Over 11 seasons, from 1963 through 1973, his Buffaloes went 67-49-2 and played in five bowl games. Among the signature wins of his tenure was a 1970 victory over fourth-ranked Penn State that ended the Nittany Lions' 31-game unbeaten streak.

Crowder also took on a second job. On July 1, 1965, he became Colorado's athletic director, succeeding Harry Carlson, and he held that post until 1984, which meant he ran the department for nearly two decades.

His honors reflect both halves of that career. He was inducted into the Colorado Sports Hall of Fame in 1990, the Oklahoma Sports Hall of Fame in 2003 and the Colorado athletic hall of fame in 2004. Crowder died in 2008.
